newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - HS barges softer, LS cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - HS barges softer, LS cargoes steady.

text.p: High sulphur cracked barges ended a touch easier on Tuesday on the back of weak bunker demand.
Barges traded at $113 fob ARA around midday, unchanged from Monday, before settling back to $109-111 a tonne.

High sulphur cracked cargoes were again fairly quiet although a cargo was offered at $108 fob NWE and 10,000 tonnes was heard done at $107 fob NWE on prompt dates. The market was tight although some dealers thought the $109 on Friday had been overplayed and that the market was closer to $105 fob NWE.
"I have my doubts about the $107 deal," said one.
Good Russian supplies also showed bearish potential.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were a touch steadier. There were unconfirmed rumours a Med buyer secured a cargo on Monday. Another deal was done Monday at high fob NWE +$2/2.25 for 50kt.
A short into a UK end user for high viscosity material has prompted a bid of $114.50 cif against an offer of $118.
One percent requirements in Septewmber look thin though one buyer, who secured 20kt at cif high cif NWE +$1.75/2 was looking for more on Monday.
The Turkish tender for delivery into Izmit by Oct 1-5 was awarded at close of business, but details have yet to emerge.
